body:
Title: Lack of aggressive context compaction / prompt caching burns the 5h and weekly quota far faster than token cost would suggest

## Summary

Even on **Gemini 3.8 Flash Low**, whose per-token price is very low, my usage burns through the **5-hour** and **weekly** rate-limit windows roughly **3x faster** than I'd expect from token cost alone. The bottleneck isn't $/token — it's that each turn appears to resend a much larger share of the conversation history than necessary, because Antigravity currently has no user-facing, configurable context compaction or prompt-caching strategy.

## Problem

- Context compaction exists internally, but it's opaque and not tunable (see prior reports: "Antigravity IDE lacks basic context compaction" and "Frustrated with aggressive context compaction before plan execution" on the Google AI Developers Forum). Users can't tell when/how aggressively it triggers, and can't adjust the trigger threshold.
- There's no documented **prompt/context caching** mechanism (TTL-based or otherwise) that would let repeated, unchanged context (system prompt, tool schemas, stable file context, earlier turns) be reused cheaply instead of being re-sent and re-billed against the rate-limit window on every turn.
- The practical effect: long-running agentic sessions (multi-file edits, iterative debugging, long tool-call chains) consume 5h/weekly quota far faster than the advertised low per-token cost of Flash models would imply, because quota consumption tracks re-sent context volume, not just genuinely new content.

## What I'd like to see (inspired by Claude Code's approach)

1. **Automatic context caching with a TTL** (e.g. ~1h) for stable prefix content (system/developer prompt, tool definitions, long-lived file context) so unchanged context isn't re-priced/re-counted against quota on every single turn.
2. **User-visible, configurable compaction** — expose a setting (e.g. in `config.json` / Agent Settings) to control compaction aggressiveness and/or a manual "compact now" trigger, instead of silent, unpredictable compaction.
3. **Quota transparency** — surface how much of a turn's consumption came from re-sent history vs. new content, so users can see the actual cost driver.
4. Optionally, a hard bound on autonomous loop iterations (e.g. cap at 10 steps before requiring explicit continuation), to prevent a single runaway agentic loop from burning a disproportionate share of the 5h/weekly window.

## Context

- Model: Gemini 3.8 Flash, including "Low" tier
- Observed: ~3x faster exhaustion of the 5h and weekly usage windows compared to what token pricing alone would predict, for long agentic sessions
- Related existing threads:
  - https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/bug-feedback-antigravity-ide-lacks-basic-context-compaction-claude-opus-4-6-is-virtually-unusable-due-to-constant-prompt-is-too-long-agent-terminations/128230
  - https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/frustrated-with-aggressive-context-compaction-before-plan-execution/167983
